C Extras

Misc C features

Enum types

Suppose you had a game with playing cards, hearts/clubs/spades/diamonds.

  • Don't just use the strings "Hearts" etc or 1/2/3/4 in the code for these different suits
  • Old C way is 
    	  #define HEARTS 1
	  #define CLUBS 2
	  #define SPADES 3
	  #define DIAMONDS 4
    -- make macros for each of these number codes, use HEARTS in your code to mean suit 1.
  • Enum version of the same is similar: 
    enum suit {HEARTS=1,CLUBS,SPADES,DIAMONDS}
    -- same numerical abbreviation but makes a new type suit for them (which is really an integer under the covers).
    -- The =1 lets the encoded numbers start at 1 not 0; default if left off is start at 0

Function pointers

  • Functions themselves can be treated as data: put in variables, pass around, call
  • Allows code to be "plugged in" to an algorithm
  • Analogy: a function pointer is like an object with no fields, one method.
  • Types of function pointer variables: take prototype 
    return_type my_fun(args)
    and transform to 
    return_type(*myfunptr)(args)
    to declare myfunptr as ptr to such a prototype 
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

int addone(int i) { return ++i; }
int subone(int i) { return --i; }

void swap(int* a, int *b) { int tmp=*a; *a=*b; *b=tmp; }
void dontswap(int* a, int *b) {  }


int main()
{
    int(*iifunptr)(int); // declares as pointer to int-to-int function

    if ( rand() % 2 ) iifunptr = addone; // equivalently, "&addone"
    else iifunptr = &subone; // equivalently, "subone"
    int val = iifunptr(5);   // note no need for * deferenence of function pointer
    printf("5 plus or minus one is %d\n",val);
    
    void(*sivoidfunptr)(int*, int*);
  
    if ( rand() % 2 ) sivoidfunptr = swap;
    else sivoidfunptr = dontswap;
    int i = 4, j = 6;
    sivoidfunptr(&i,&j); 
    printf("i and j swapped or not? i=%d, j=%d\n",i,j);

}

Function pointers and the qsort() library function

  • qsort() needs the comparison operator (less, equal, greater)
  • Solution: pass it a function pointer which is that comparison op 
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <stdio.h>


int compare(const void *a, const void *b)
{   // must cast to actual type
    return *(int *)a - *(int *)b;
}

int main()
{
    int a[10], i;
    
    // load array with random numbers
    for (i = 0;i < 10;i++) a[i] = rand() % 10;
    
    qsort(a,10,sizeof(int),compare); // equivalent to &compare here -- pointer to function
    
    for (i = 0;i < 10;i++) printf ("%d\n",a[i]);
}
  • compare is the function here, note it is the 4th parameter to qsort()
  • The & on the name is optional, C knows it needs to pass the address.
  • C has no generic types, so compare always needs to take two void * pointers in its prototype
  • But you as user know the type you used, so use a typecast in your compare.
  • The a/b types are pointer types since function parameters need to be of fixed size (subtle point).
  • qsort's prototype shows a function pointer type declaration: 
    void qsort (void* base, size_t num, size_t size,
            int (*compar)(const void*,const void*));
EXERCISE: Write a program to create an array of doubles between 0 and 1, then write two compare functions so you can sort them in ascending and descending orders. [solution]

Union types

  • Union data is "this OR that", not "this AND that" of structs
  • Unions are generally used inside of structures to let some fields share space
  • Space efficiency is important in low-level programming

Example 

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

struct ssn_union_jhed {
    int type; // a tag: 0 = JHED 1 = SSN
    union {
        long int ssn;
        char jhed[8];  // put jhed OVER ssn in memory (shared)
    } the_union;
};

// non-union alternative to above which uses more memory
// struct ssn_or_jhed {
//    int type;
//    long int ssn;
//    char jhed[8];
//};

int main()
{
    struct ssn_union_jhed suj;
    long int myssn = 232982374;
    char myjhed[8]= "ssmith26";
    
    suj.type = (rand() % 2); // flip coin: SSN or JHED?
    
    if (suj.type) suj.the_union.ssn = myssn;
    else strcpy(suj.the_union.jhed,myjhed);

// set a breakpoint here and print suj to see whats there
// test run gave this:
// (gdb) print suj
// $1 = {type = 1, the_union = {ssn = 232982374, jhed = "f\a\343\r\000\000\000"}}
}

Macros

We have seen some simple #define macros before: 

#define SIZE 30
  • Macros can also take arguments: 
    #define MACRO_NAME(args) (macro expression)
  • Example: 
    #define CIRCUM(x, y) (2 * (x) + 2 * (y))
  • Make sure to put args x, y in () in body
    -- C is pretty much doing string substitution here, precedence can change if not careful
  • Macros just inline the code, a special pre-processor cpp runs over your code and expands them.
  • So, 
    CIRCUM(3+4,33)
    expands to 
    (2 * (3+4) + 2 * (33))
  • #undef CIRCUM -- in lines after undef the CIRCUM macro will not work

Macros for Conditional compilation

Useful for portability (different platforms need different code) and for debugging

Debug flag is a common usage 

#include <stdio.h>
#define DEBUG 1 // keep line in when debugging, comment out when not
main()
{
    int w = 10;
    // ... lots of code ...
    #if DEBUG     // or #ifdef DEBUG, has same meaning here
    printf("Debugging w: w = %d\n",w); //  debug code only included when DEBUG defined
    #endif
    // ... more code ...
}
  • The compiler needs to be able to figure out the condition result
    -- don't put program variables in #if condition

Example you have seen of this in a .h file: 

#ifndef HW3       // means "If HW3 is not a current macro definition"
#define HW3       // it is now (and the macro body is empty, its only serving as a flag)

// Put all of the intended hw3.h file headers here

#endif
  • If HW3 is already a defined macro the header will not be included
  • Means no header will be included twice (which would be bad, double definition error)
